newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian CFE sees higher 1997 profit.
newsitem.headline: Belgian CFE sees higher 1997 profit.

text.p: Belgian construction and dredging group CFE told shareholders on Wednesday it expected slightly higher 1997 earnings.

"Taking account of activity forecasts for 1997, the level of turnover and sales should be higher than in 1996 and results should progress slightly compared with the previous exercise," CFE Chairman Walter Vanden Avenne told the company's annual shareholders meeting.
A text of his comments was made available by the company.

CFE sales in 1996 slipped to 7.32 from 8.20 billion Belgian francs. Group net profit nearly halved to 134 from 252 million francs. The company blamed a fall in French and international activities and the deconsolidation of a Hong Kong unit as well as aggressive competition compressing margins.
"On the Belgian construction market, CFE does not see any improvement in the short term...," Vanden Avenne said.

Elsewhere, he said, the picture was brighter. In the Netherlands, CFE said it was setting up a new unit, CFE Nederland BV, regrouping all its activities to take advantage of publicly-sponsored civil engineering projects.
Its east European building activities and Groupe Verelst unit would also help CFE sales in 1997, it said.
In dredging, "the DEME group expects 1997 and 1998 to be exceptional in terms of volume and use of its fleet."
Belgian dredging firm DEME NV is 39 percent held by CFE. Belgian holding company Ackermans & Van Haaren also has a 35.5 percent stake in DEME.
